name: blender-to-roblox-import
description: Take a model from Blender into Roblox Studio as clean, game-ready MeshParts - build to Roblox scale, colour with vertex colours (materials do not transfer), export FBX with the right settings, have the user run File > Import 3D, then fix the import automatically (100x scale, hidden PivotOffsets, PrimaryPart, welds, model scale) and verify. Use whenever the user wants a Blender model, pet, prop or accessory brought into Studio, asks why an import came in huge/rotated/grey/falling apart, or wants to replace an existing model with a new Blender version.
---

# Blender -> Roblox Studio import

## What can and cannot be automated
- Automated: building/painting/exporting in Blender (`execute_blender_code`), and every fix-up step in Studio (Edit-mode Luau).
- NOT automatable (tested): the import itself.
  - `AssetImportService` is not available to scripts.
  - `AssetService:CreateEditableMesh` + `CreateMeshPartAsync` renders, but the MeshPart has an empty MeshId, is not saved with the place and `Clone()` loses the mesh.
  - `AssetService:CreateAssetAsync(..., Enum.AssetType.Mesh)` fails: "CreateAssetAsync and CreateAssetVersionAsync are not available yet".
  - Blender and Studio share no file path; mesh data would have to pass through chat (too large for real models).
- So: ask the user to run **File > Import 3D** once per model. Do everything else yourself.

## 1. Build in Blender
- 1 Blender unit = 1 stud. Check real sizes (N panel). Keep a consistent size across a family of models.
- Front faces **-Y**, up is **+Z**, origin at **bottom centre**.
- Apply transforms (Ctrl+A > All Transforms, or `bpy.ops.object.transform_apply`).
- One object per part (body, ears, legs, accessories). The main body will become the PrimaryPart.
- Keep each mesh under ~20k triangles.
- Axis mapping on import: Blender (x, y, z) -> Roblox (-x, z, y). Front -Y becomes Roblox -Z; Blender -X side becomes Roblox +X. This is a rotation, not a mirror, so faces painted while looking at the -Y side read correctly.
- After `bpy.ops.wm.read_homefile(use_empty=True)` the context is broken for the rest of that script: build with `bmesh` + `bpy.data` (not `bpy.ops` / `bpy.context.active_object`).

## 2. Colour with vertex colours
Blender materials/procedural shaders do not transfer. Use a colour attribute per mesh:

```python
import bpy
def fill(ob, rgb255, name='Col'):
    me = ob.data
    a = me.color_attributes.get(name) or me.color_attributes.new(name, 'BYTE_COLOR', 'CORNER')
    c = tuple(x / 255 for x in rgb255) + (1.0,)
    for d in a.data:
        d.color_srgb = c
    me.color_attributes.active_color = a
    me.color_attributes.render_color_index = list(me.color_attributes).index(a)
```

Painted details (eyes, mouths, markings) without 3D geometry:
1. Back up the mesh first (hidden copy).
2. Subdivide only the flat faces that will be painted (`bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges(..., use_grid_fill=True)`); go finer (~0.025 studs) only where detail lives to save triangles. Mark the mesh with a custom property so it is not subdivided twice.
3. For each face on that side, test its centre against 2D shapes (circles, ellipses, thick polylines) traced from the reference image in pixel space, mapped to model coordinates; set all its corners to that colour.
4. Reset the painted side to the base colour before repainting (blends are not idempotent).
5. Verify without a render: bin face centres into a grid and print an ASCII map of the colours.
- Gotcha: reading byte colours through bmesh already gives sRGB - do not convert again.

## 3. Export FBX

```python
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
for o in parts: o.hide_set(False); o.select_set(True)
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath=path, use_selection=True, object_types={'MESH'},
    colors_type='SRGB', apply_unit_scale=True, mesh_smooth_type='FACE',
    add_leaf_bones=False, bake_anim=False)
bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=blend_path)
```
- Export only the model's meshes (no lights, cameras, backups). Object names become part names in Studio - export with the final names.

## 4. User step
Tell the user exactly: "In Studio: File > Import 3D > pick <file>.fbx > default options > Import into Workspace, then tell me." Do not continue until they confirm.

## 5. Fix the import (Edit-mode Luau)
Known import defects:
- Everything is **100x too big**.
- Every part carries a **rotated PivotOffset ~100 studs away**; without a fix `PivotTo` rotates the model 90 deg and throws it far away.
- No PrimaryPart, no welds.

Generic fix-up (replace an existing model, keeping its data):

```lua
local CHS = game:GetService("ChangeHistoryService")
local function FixImport(imp, bodyName, old, targetParent)
	local rec = CHS:TryBeginRecording("FixImport")
	local body = imp:FindFirstChild(bodyName, true)
	local bodyCF = body.CFrame
	local baseCF = CFrame.new(old and old.PrimaryPart.Position or body.Position / 100) * bodyCF.Rotation
	local m = Instance.new("Model"); m.Name = old and old.Name or imp.Name
	local main, parts = nil, {}
	for _, p in ipairs(imp:GetDescendants()) do
		if p:IsA("BasePart") then
			local rel = bodyCF:ToObjectSpace(p.CFrame)
			rel = (rel - rel.Position) + rel.Position / 100
			local c = p:Clone()
			for _, ch in ipairs(c:GetChildren()) do if ch:IsA("JointInstance") or ch:IsA("WeldConstraint") then ch:Destroy() end end
			c.PivotOffset = CFrame.new()
			c.Size = p.Size / 100
			c.CFrame = baseCF * rel
			if p == body then c.Name = "MainPart"; main = c end
			local src = old and old:FindFirstChild(c.Name)
			if src and src:IsA("BasePart") then -- copy behaviour, NOT Color (keeps vertex colours untinted)
				for _, k in ipairs({"Material","Anchored","CanCollide","CanTouch","CanQuery","CastShadow","Massless","Transparency"}) do c[k] = src[k] end
			end
			c.Parent = m; table.insert(parts, c)
		end
	end
	m.PrimaryPart = main; m.WorldPivot = main.CFrame
	for _, c in ipairs(parts) do
		if c ~= main then
			local w = Instance.new("Weld"); w.Name = c.Name; w.Part0 = main; w.Part1 = c
			w.C0 = main.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(c.CFrame); w.Parent = main
		end
	end
	if old then m:ScaleTo(old:GetScale()) end
	for _, c in ipairs(parts) do c.PivotOffset = CFrame.new() end -- again after ScaleTo
	m.WorldPivot = main.CFrame
	for _, w in ipairs(main:GetChildren()) do if w:IsA("Weld") then w.C0 = main.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(w.Part1.CFrame); w.C1 = CFrame.new() end end
	if old then
		for _, ch in ipairs(old:GetChildren()) do if not ch:IsA("BasePart") then ch:Clone().Parent = m end end -- settings folders etc.
		for k, v in pairs(old:GetAttributes()) do if not k:find("^RBX_") then m:SetAttribute(k, v) end end
		old.Name = old.Name .. " (backup)"; old.Parent = game.ServerStorage -- never delete the original
	end
	m.Parent = targetParent; imp:Destroy()
	if rec then CHS:FinishRecording(rec, Enum.FinishRecordingOperation.Commit) end
	return m
end
```
- Inspect first (read-only): list the imported parts with sizes/positions and the old model's parts, scale, PrimaryPart and attributes. Confirm the orientation matches (e.g. ear/tail sides) before swapping.
- Adapt: the body name, which children to copy, the target folder.

## 6. Verify
1. Compare every part's size and MainPart-relative position against the old model (max error should be ~0), check the part count, and check `GetPivot().Position == MainPart.Position` and `PivotOffset == CFrame.new()`.
2. Visual check in Edit mode: a temporary ScreenGui in **StarterGui** (CoreGui does not show in the edit viewport) with a ViewportFrame + Camera, a clone pivoted to the origin, camera at the front (-Z) looking +Z; `screen_capture`; crop/zoom the capture if small. Remove the preview afterwards.
3. Playtest wherever the model is used (UI cards, world, egg/shop previews).

## Gotchas checklist
- Huge model -> the 100x import scale. Spinning/offset model -> PivotOffsets not reset.
- Grey/washed colours -> exported without sRGB vertex colours, or the part Color is tinting them.
- Falling apart -> missing welds / not anchored.
- One command per step; Edit-mode Luau fails during Play - stop Play before editing.
- Always back up the old model and the unpainted mesh; use ChangeHistoryService so the user can undo.
